title: Defender of the Crown
japaneseTitle: ディフェンダー・オブ・ザ・クラウン
shortDescription: Cinemaware's breathtaking interactive cinematic strategy game that showcased the revolutionary audiovisual power of the 16-bit Commodore Amiga.
historicalSignificance: Widely regarded as the Amiga's first genuine killer app, Jim Sachs's stunning 32-color pixel illustrations and digital orchestral score stunned the computer industry and proved 16-bit multimedia computers were the future of interactive art.

editorialContent.overview: Set in medieval England in 1149 AD following the assassination of the King, players assume the role of a Saxon lord (such as Wilfred of Ivanhoe) fighting Norman invaders and rival lords to reunite the kingdom.
editorialContent.gameplay: Blends turn-based territorial conquest with real-time action minigames: tactical jousting tournaments to win land and honor, castle sieges using catapult boulder physics, and tense indoor swordplay duels.
editorialContent.technicalInnovation: Leveraged the Amiga 1000's custom OCS chipset (Denise and Paula) to display 32 simultaneous colors from a 4,096-color palette and 4-channel 8-bit PCM audio, rendering IBM PC and Apple II visuals obsolete overnight.
editorialContent.culturalImpact: Demonstrated that home computer games could deliver Hollywood cinematic production values, founding Cinemaware's legendary interactive movie era.
editorialContent.preservationNotes: Preserved on original 3.5-inch Amiga floppy disks and ported to numerous contemporary home computer platforms.

verifiedFactualData.sales: Over 1 million copies sold across all computer platforms

technicalSpecs.resolution: 320 x 200 (32 simultaneous colors via OCS palette)
